explanation: The I54M substitution in the flap region reduces lopinavir binding despite minimal volume loss because the replacement of isoleucine's branched, rigid hydrophobic side chain with methionine's longer, more flexible thioether chain disrupts critical van der Waals contacts that stabilize the inhibitor-protease complex at ~6.7 Å from the ligand. Although methionine maintains overall hydrophobicity adequate for general binding, its conformational flexibility and reduced local packing density in this spatially constrained flap pocket create sub-optimal van der Waals complementarity with lopinavir's surface, translating the energetic penalty into the observed weakening of binding affinity.
